correctness.rationale: The Zimin interleaving recursion rigorously partitions suffixes by initial symbol; preserving the projected lexicographic order gives the exact suffix-array recurrence. The a1 alternation proves that suffix-prefix comparisons retain their order under circular wrap. Predecessor characters and the primary-row recurrence give the exact transform. Special boundary n=2 has merged a1 blocks; n>=3 has 2n-1 runs. Independent finite checks reproduce complete rotations through n=9 and all suffixes through n=11. No computational extrapolation is used as proof.

originality.rationale: Searches and implication-level comparisons found no source covering the all-rank Zimin suffix-array recurrence, exact symbol-by-symbol cyclic BWT, and primary row. Earlier work defines the BWT, classifies one-block-per-letter transforms, and gives transform expressions for different recursive families. The rank-three instance abacaba is expressly already known. The inaccessible full text of one close general BWT paper is a disclosed priority risk, not treated as proven noncoverage.

value.rationale: A closed complete BWT output and suffix-array permutation for all ranks of a classical recursive-word family is a motivated compression/indexing invariant, not an arbitrary finite slice. It realizes logarithmic RLE length with exact blocks and a known primary row for exponentially long inputs; the full structure does not follow from the elementary n-symbol run lower bound or earlier single-instance BWT examples. It does not purport to optimize over all words.
